HR Employee Attrition Analysis

Understanding employee turnover, workforce demographics, job satisfaction, and retention risk through a four-page Power BI dashboard.

The project examines turnover, workforce composition, job satisfaction, overtime, salary-related indicators, and possible retention risks. It looks for patterns and associations, not proven causes.

The dashboard answers nine business questions for HR leadership.

    Root causes and attrition risk

    DAX measures and their business purpose

    These are proposed examples. Adjust table and column names, data types, and filters to match the actual Power BI model. They are not the original formulas unless confirmed from the PBIX file.

    Related concepts (include if used in the implementation)

    • Filter context: each measure recalculates for the slicers and visual axes applied.
    • Slicers: let viewers filter by age group, gender, or marital status.
    • Drill-through: passes the selected job role to a detail page.
    • Relationships and calculated columns: e.g. age bins or tenure groups.

    Methodology and limitations

    Typical workflow proposed, not verified

    1. Understand the business problem
    2. Inspect the HR dataset
    3. Clean and validate the data
    4. Define measures and KPIs
    5. Build Power BI visualizations
    6. Add slicers and drill-through
    7. Validate calculations against source records
    8. Interpret the results
    9. Develop recommendations

    Limitations

    • Screenshots do not expose the full dataset or the original DAX.
    • Correlation does not establish causation.
    • Small groups can produce unstable attrition percentages.
    • Aggregated values change when slicers are applied.
    • Employee-level information should be anonymized before public sharing.
